rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Layout, cut, form, fit and weld a circular ring of a specified diameter.
Demonstrate safety awareness in the welding workplace.
Layout, Cut, Form, Fit, Weld a simple rectangular sheet metal box.
objectives: Interpret and apply welding blueprints;
Illustrate welding joints and perform material layout;
Explain and apply geometric construction;
Explain and apply parallel line development;
Explain and apply radial line development;
Illustrate fit up of components for welding in the proper sequences to standard;
Select, understand, and properly use welding jigs, fixtures and holding devices;
Illustrate control of weld distortion and defects;
Demonstrate proper methods and techniques for straightening;
Demonstrate rigging techniques;
Material handling safe practices
Practice the basics of SMAW, GMAW, GTAW, FCAW, Plasma and oxy-fuel cutting.
rows.objectives_lead: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to:

rows.title: Basic Welding Skills Laboratory
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety awareness in the welding workplace.
Demonstrates achievement of self directed goals.
objectives: Illustrate beginning skill and knowledge development in the welding process chosen by the student to study;
Shielded Metal Arc (SMAW);
Gas Tungsten Arc (GTAW);
Gas Metal Arc (GMAW);
Flux Core Arc (FCAW);
Demonstrate safe and proper use of equipment;
Practice skills appropriate to entry-level employment in the metal trades.
Demonstrate development and completion of self-directed skills development goals
Perform Basic Welding in the Horizontal (2G and 2F) positions
rows.objectives_lead: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to:

rows.title: Certification Preparation
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety awareness in the welding workplace.
Demonstrates self directed goals achievement.
objectives: Display skills required to pass a welding certification test;
American Welding Society D1.1;
American society of Mechanical Engineers Section IX;
American Petroleum Institute 1104;
List the requirements to take the specified certification test;
Construct coupons required to pass the tests;
Employ understanding of destructive and non-destructive examination of test welds;
Identify discontinuities that will lead to test failure.
rows.objectives_lead: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to:

rows.title: Introduction to Welding
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safe use of SMAW equipment.
Demonstrate safety awareness in the welding workplace.
Identify welding electrodes used for common industrial welding processes/applications.
objectives: Demonstrate safe and proper use of equipment:
Shielded Metal Arc (SMAW);
Gas Tungsten Arc (GTAW);
Gas Metal Arc (GMAW);
Flux Core Arc (FCAW);
Oxy-fuel welding and brazing;
Plasma and oxy-fuel cutting
Apply gas welding sheet steel in flat position;
Practice GMAW, FCAW, SMAW weld steel in the flat position;
Practice GTAW weld steel, stainless, and aluminum in the flat position;
Demonstrate braze welding of a simple part;
Use plasma and oxy-fuel to cut manually and with a machine;
Safely operate welding support equipment;
Identify and list career potentials in the welding industry.
rows.objectives_lead: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to:

rows.title: Welding Workplace Safety
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety awareness in the welding workplace.
Identify and describe the Focus Four Hazards.
Learn an OSHA 10 Safety Certification.
objectives: Explain OSHA safety standards as they relate to welding/construction workplace safety;
Describe employer/employee construction safety rights and responsibilities;
Identify the focus four hazards;
Explain personal protective equipment usage and requirements;
Identify health hazards in the welding/construction workplace;
Describe materials handling equipment and safe usage;
Explain hand and power tool safe usage;
Describe safe scaffold usage;
Explain safe operations around cranes, derricks, hoists, elevators & conveyors;
Recognize safe operations around excavations;
Identify safe operations around stairways and ladders;
rows.objectives_lead: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to:

rows.title: Introduction to Women’s Studies
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the multiple types of feminism that currently exist in the United States.
Illustrate connections between global, national, and local issues in relationship to women’s experiences and human rights.
Recognize the ways in which social institutions and power structures impact women’s lives.
objectives: Explore the theoretical background of the interdisciplinary study of women;
Analyze the impact of race, class, age, ethnicity and sexual orientation on women’s lives;
Synthesize material from primary and secondary sources in order to analyze the role of women in the United States;
Explore the process of transforming social structures through feminism;
Examine the effect of the social and political women’s movements in the United States;
Investigate contemporary social problems for women in the United States;
Examine one’s own personal position and how it relates to the rest of society.
rows.objectives_lead: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to:

rows.title: General Work Experience
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate development of professional work skills at the workplace.
Evaluate workplace performance in a reflective essay.
objectives: Develop college-level, on-the-job learning objectives, in collaboration with the instructor and workplace supervisor, which are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-based (SMART).
Apply professional work skills at the workplace.
Analyze job requirements, employer expectations, and skills required for promotional opportunities.
Evaluate workplace performance to identify strengths and areas for improvement that will increase employability.
Complete academic and career pathway activities to assess interests, develop career awareness, and plan for a career.
rows.objectives_lead: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to:

rows.title: Women's Weight Training 1
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate appropriate weight room etiquette.
Demonstrate proper form when executing beginning-level weight training exercises.
Express weight training’s benefits and effect on long-term health.
objectives: Demonstrate how to utilize the weight training equipment safely and proper gym etiquette
Identify the basic musculoskeletal anatomical features of the human female body
Describe the kinesiology movements of the female body
Explain the fundamental tenets of the weight training prescription
Discuss body composition, assessment, and data interpretation
Articulate appropriate and achievable personal weight training goals
Perform a personal assessment of physical conditioning/fitness and weight training program

rows.lead: Upon the completion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate an increase in their flexibility.
Demonstrate proper alignment in beginning level asanas.
Utilize various breathing techniques used in a yoga practice.
objectives: Describe the physical and mental benefits of yoga
Demonstrate basic Hatha Yoga poses designed to strengthen and tone the body
Use relaxation and breathing techniques for personal benefit
Identify elementary human anatomy
Discuss the changes that have occurred in personal development

Demonstrate and name 2-4 intermediate/advanced yoga poses in both English and Sanskrit.
objectives: Perform advanced Yoga poses/asana with proper body mechanics.
Perform breathing techniques during an advanced Yoga practice.
Demonstrate relaxation, meditation, mantra and guided relaxation exercises.
Describe the eight limbs of Yoga using proper Sanskrit terminology.
Analyze and evaluate the benefits of advanced Yoga practice.
